Once a root was found, a linear factor and hence a quadratic factor could be found, followed by 3 linear factors.

notes.1a: Many candidates were able to obtain full marks, correctly identifying the values of a , b and c . Some candidates had problems dealing with the factor 2 x + a to find the value of a . ( )
notes.1b: Most candidates were able to identify the critical values to the appropriate level of accuracy, but some made errors relating these values to the given inequality. Some candidates omitted x 1.2.
notes.5a: A new addition to the syllabus, most candidates appeared familiar with the form of the circle equation given and were able to write down the coordinates of the centre of the circle. Many candidates were then able to find the gradient of the line from the centre of the circle to the given point and then find the gradient of the tangent at the given point. Although many correct solutions were see n , many candidates did not appear to read the demand of the question fully and hence did not give the tangent equation in the required form.
notes.5b: Very few correct solutions were seen. Solutions which contained a diagram made it easier for candidates to consider the distance between the centres of the circles and the sum of the radii.
notes.7a: Not all candidates appeared to carefully read that t he requirement of the question was to find the value of sin , θ not the value of θ . Use of the sine rule for the area of a triangle was needed to find the answer of sin θ = .
notes.7b: Using the method for finding the area of a circle segment was attempted by most candidates, who were able to find the correct value of θ . Many correct final answers for the arc length of the arc AB were seen.
notes.8a: Most candidates were able to obtain the correct y - coordinates of the points A and B .
notes.8b: The most straightforward method of solution was to find the area of the trapezium that could be formed and subtract the area under the curve. Some candidates made the problem more complex than necessary by finding the equation of the line AB first and then using subtraction and integration. Errors were more likely to occur using this method. Few completely correct solutions were seen due to errors in integration, application of the limits and subtraction.
notes.9ai: M any candidates made both algebraic and arithmetic slips and were unable to complete the square correctly. The main problem appeared to be the negative coefficient of x .
notes.9aii: Very few correct solutions were seen. Candidates needed to be able to determine the coordinates of the stationary point on the curve making use of their answer to part (i) as required by use of the word ‘Hence’. A comparison of the given domain with the x - coordinate of the stationary point showed that this was included in the given domain, so no inverse function.
notes.9bi: Very few completely correct sketches were seen. Most candidates did not know the correct shape of the curve and of those that did, many did not sketch it over the given domain. Some were aware of the equation of the asymptote and the coordinates of the points of intersection, but these only scored marks if a correct shape had been sketched. Candidates should be aware of the given domain when sketching graphs.
notes.9bii: Most candidates were able to use a correct method and find the inverse function using the correct notation.
notes.9biii: Very few correct solutions were seen for either the range or the domain of the inverse function. F ew candidates had a correct sketch which could be used to hel p with this part.
notes.10a: Most candidates were able to the correct vector as required, making correct use of the given ratio.
notes.10b: Few completely correct solutions were seen. Candidates were expected to find another expression for OE , introducing another scalar quantity. Like vectors could then be compared and the values of each scalar quantity found. Although few candidates gained full marks, many candidates were able to obtain intermediate marks provided they had shown their work clearly.
notes.11a: It was essential that candidates find the velocity of the particle at both stages of the motion. Many candidates did this and were able to gain marks for correct differentiation. Few correct sketches were seen. Candidates did not use the fact that there was a maximum point when t = 2 to help with the quadratic part of the sketch. Whilst some quadratic curves were sketched, many candidates did not realise that when t = 3, a straight line needed to be sketched. Of those candidates that did sketch a straight line, most finished their straight line on the horizontal axis.
notes.11b: Very few correct solutions were seen, mainly due to the fact that an incorrect sketch had been drawn so referencing what was needed was difficult. A substitution of t = 3 gave the distance for the first part of the journey. Use of the area of a trapezium was then needed to find an expression for the second part of the journey and hence make use of the given relationship to find k. Many candidates did not attempt this part of the question.
